Drawing on the warm relationships we have built with our feline and canine friends and the experience we have gained over time, we have thought of everything your furry friend needs to have a wonderful time while you are away. We have created a happy place to stay and socialise so that the most precious members of our family feel at home.

t146: We answer your questions before your little friend’s stay.
t148: Where do our feline and canine friends stay?
t149: We do everything we can to make their stay comfortable in a detached villa in Koşuyolu. We welcome our feline friends on the upper floor of the villa and our canine friends on the lower floor. We take care to provide dedicated spaces for both.
t150: We don’t restrict our feline friends’ free spirits, either. We provide space that suits their natural desire to do things their own way. Depending on their owner’s preference or their own, they can enjoy themselves in their own space or in shared areas.
t151: Is anaesthesia used for pets receiving grooming services?
t152: Even if our little guests are feisty or shy, we patiently complete their grooming and never use anaesthesia.
t154: We are open every day of the week from 09:00–18:30. Opening hours may vary on public holidays.
t155: Please contact us on 0532 529 01 76 for check-in and check-out times, collection arrangements and pricing terms.

t170: Frequently Asked Questions | Loft Pet House
t172: We can’t take your place, but we can make sure they don’t feel your absence.
t173: How do you accommodate cats who aren’t sociable and don’t get along with other cats?
t174: We also offer a solution for our feline friends who prefer spending time on their own and aren’t very interested in socialising. Once a separate area has been disinfected, we let them spend around 2–3 hours there on their own, away from the other cats. We have solutions for free spirits, too. ;)
t175: Do you take the dogs for walks? For how long each day?
t176: Although they spend plenty of time in our outdoor area during the day, we never skip our 30-minute walks in the morning, at midday and in the evening.
t177: Do you collect our pets, or should we bring them to you?
t178: That is entirely up to you. You can bring your friends to us yourself or use our transfer service for a reasonable fee. We will arrange whichever option suits you.
t179: Can we see our pets at any time?
t180: You can contact us whenever you want to know how your friend is doing. Let’s plan video calls and updates during their stay together.
t182: Does the veterinarian also provide services for pets who are not staying with you?
t183: No, our veterinarian provides services for our friends staying at our hotel. While on site, the veterinarian carries out routine health checks on our little guests. Other than that, we do not provide services for pets visiting during the day for health checks, vaccinations or similar needs.
t184: Why should we choose Loft Pet House?
t185: Above all, we never compromise on trustworthiness. Many individuals and organisations open pet hotels as businesses without completing the necessary paperwork or obtaining the required permits. In contrast, Loft Pet House operates with licences approved by the municipality and the Ministry of Agriculture. We have completed all the legal procedures required to open a pet hotel in full and through lawful channels. You can review our certificates for more information.

t204: Our beloved companions, who enter our lives with their sweet, endearing ways and win our hearts from the moment they arrive, need training.
t205: Although these beloved members of our family are domesticated, they descend from the wolf (Canis Lupus). These animals live according to a hierarchical system. They divide themselves into ranks such as alpha, beta and omega, fight if necessary to become the alpha female or alpha male, and the winner takes the highest rank, becoming the pack’s alpha. The dogs we welcome into our families cannot see us as family members such as a mother or father.
t206: At home, they see us as a pack and, when left to their own devices, instinctively create a pack structure in their minds. When this structure leads to undesirable outcomes, we as owners struggle and problems begin to emerge.
t207: If they have placed themselves in the alpha position, they will not obey, will not easily give up this position and will make things difficult for family members. For example, if you tell your dog not to get on the sofa, they may become stubborn and, if necessary, show their strength, growl or bare their teeth to challenge you. In such situations, if families do not seek professional support and try to handle things without enough knowledge, their inexperience can bring them close to giving up their dogs altogether. Training is the best and kindest way to communicate this to them and establish their place within the pack structure.
t208: On the surface, it may seem to consist only of commands such as sit, lie down, stand and stay, but to them it is more than just commands. As long as they follow the commands they receive, you can understand that they have accepted you as the alpha and know their place in the pack.
t209: Whatever animal you care for, you need to understand their world and their nature.
